many zeros in Re s < 12 . Unconditionally, we are able to deduce the following
quantitative results by similar methods in [8].

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Because f ignores simple xi zeros but retains each multiple zero with multiplicity reduced by one, symmetry and Littlewood turn its zeros into a quantitative certificate for the distinct-zero deficit N-N_d.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Littlewood's lemma expresses a weighted zero sum of fB as an integral of log|fB|; the unit states that simple xi zeros are not zeros of f whereas a multiple xi zero contributes with multiplicity one less, so symmetry lower-bounds the sum by a multiple of N(T)-N_d(T), and Jensen bounds that deficit by an L^2 mean of fB.
directed.conceptual_reading: Multiplicity loss is encoded as zeros of an auxiliary detector, then transformed from a discrete deficit into an analytic mean-square optimization problem.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The chain f-zero multiplicity → symmetric weighted sum → Littlewood logarithm → Jensen mean square bridges distinctness to mollified analysis.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The bound is not numerical until the later differential-polynomial rewrite and parameter evaluation; exact contour constants and admissibility conditions matter.
directed.uncertainty: The detector mechanism is explicit, but contour shifts, multiplicity weights, normalization constants, and the limsup display require scan verification.
